692602d1df29.title_raw: Platform & Site Reliability Engineering Internship - Summer 2027
692602d1df29.description_html:
Immuta is the Data Authorization Company, helping the world’s largest organizations control who, and what, can access their data.

The way enterprises access data is fundamentally changing. Organizations are racing to put data to work across analytics and AI, while AI copilots and agents are emerging as an entirely new class of data consumer. Traditional approaches built around tickets, static permissions, and manual approvals were not designed for this speed, scale, or complexity.

Immuta provides the authorization layer for modern data and AI. Our platform enables organizations to provision governed access to data by policy, by request, and dynamically for AI agents, so people and AI can access the data they need while enterprises maintain security, compliance, and control.

For Chief Data Officers, that means making enterprise data dramatically easier to access and use without giving up governance. For AI leaders, it means giving AI agents secure, governed access to enterprise data so they can move from experimentation into production.

Founded in 2015, Immuta is trusted by Fortune 500 companies and government agencies worldwide.

  • Our technology ecosystem includes Snowflake, Databricks, AWS, Microsoft Azure, Google Cloud, Okta, ServiceNow, Teradata, Alation, Atlan, and Starburst — connecting Immuta to the data, cloud, identity, and enterprise platforms powering modern data and AI environments.
  • Immuta has been recognized by Forbes as a top American startup employer, by Inc. Magazine and Built In as one of the best workplaces, and by Fast Company as one of the world’s most innovative companies.
  • Immuta has raised $263 million from investors including NightDragon, Snowflake, Databricks, ServiceNow, Citi Ventures, Dell Technologies Capital, DFJ Growth, IAG, Intel Capital, March Capital, Okta Ventures, StepStone, Ten Eleven Ventures, and Wipro Ventures.
  • We operate as a hybrid workplace with offices in Boston, MA; Columbus, OH; and College Park, MD.

ABOUT THE TEAM

The Site Reliability Engineering team helps keep Immuta’s products reliable, deployable, and maintainable in production. The team builds software and automation, works with AWS and other cloud services, and improves how applications are released, operated, monitored, and supported.

In other words, Site Reliability Engineering sits at the intersection of software engineering and operations. As an intern, you’ll work alongside engineers who build the systems and tools that help software run reliably at scale. You’ll learn how applications move from code to deployed services and how teams improve production systems over time.

YOUR INTERNSHIP

At Immuta, interns are treated like members of the team. You’ll join the team’s regular workflow, contribute to real work, and take on responsibilities that reflect your skills and the team’s priorities.

The exact projects will depend on what the team is working on next summer, but you can expect to:

Join the Site Reliability Engineering team as an engineer, rather than working on a separate intern-only project. Build software and services that support the deployment, operation, and maintenance of Immuta’s products. Work with teammates to improve how software is released, operated, monitored, and maintained. Gain experience connecting software development with cloud services, production systems, and reliability. Apply your programming and problem-solving skills to practical systems and infrastructure challenges. Learn how engineers investigate issues, improve systems, and make software more reliable over time. Take ownership of well-scoped work, communicate your progress, and ask questions when you need context or support.

TOOLS & TECHNOLOGIES

Depending on your role, you may work with:

Go AWS and other cloud services Software deployment and maintenance workflows Production systems, reliability, monitoring, and troubleshooting practices Cloud infrastructure, containerization, or infrastructure tooling APIs and backend services AI-enabled tools and workflows used by your team You do not need to know every tool listed above. We’re looking for a strong foundation, curiosity, and the ability to learn.

WHAT WE’RE LOOKING FOR

A foundation in software engineering and experience with at least one programming language. Interest in learning new software, systems, and technologies, including Go. Interest in the broader software lifecycle, including building, deploying, operating, and maintaining applications. Strong problem-solving, communication, and collaboration skills. Experience beyond coursework, such as building or deploying an application, an internship, a hackathon, or a side project, is a plus. At Immuta, our goal is to help bridge the gap between personal and professional growth, so that our team members can be well and thrive personally and professionally. After all, great professional success stories rarely happen without great personal success stories! Our generous benefits package given to all full time employees includes:
  • 100% employer paid Healthcare (Medical, Dental, Vision) premiums for you and your dependents (including Domestic Partners)
  • Stock Options
  • Paid parental leave (Both Maternity and Paternity)
  • Unlimited Paid time off (U.S. based positions)
  • Learning and Development Resources

6985c8a6c2f7.title: Agent Engineering Intern (Los Altos)
6985c8a6c2f7.description_html:
Los Altos, CA · Engineering · Internship · Semester/quarter or summer · Fully in-person

 

Company Overview

In July 2026, Cheiron announced an $8 million seed round led by Menlo Ventures, bringing total funding to $13 million to date, with the backing and strategic support of industry veterans including Moderna co-founder and MIT Institute Professor Robert Langer, former Pfizer Chief Medical Officer Freda Lewis-Hall, Chai Discovery co-founder and CEO Josh Meier, former Starbucks CEO Laxman Narasimhan, and former Apple AI chief John Giannandrea.

 

Cheiron is building the first AI-native operating system designed to represent an entire drug program as a single connected system. The company's platform helps biopharma teams represent, reason over, and stress-test the full state of a drug development program, including the claims, evidence, assumptions, risks, decisions, and commitments that determine whether a therapy advances. In less than six months since launch, Cheiron has been adopted by tens of thousands of biopharma professionals and deployed by major drug developers, and is already used by 7 of Korea's top 10 biopharma companies.

 

Cheiron is expanding into pharmaceutical CMC (Chemistry, Manufacturing, and Controls) teams. CMC governs how a drug is made, tested, and kept consistent across its entire commercial life. The work involves hundreds of regulatory commitments, post-approval changes, and cross-market submissions. Today it runs on documents, spreadsheets, and institutional memory. Cheiron augments manual workflows with a CMC regulatory-specific intelligence and reasoning layer.

 

Founded in 2024 by Stanford-trained AI researchers. The team includes leaders with combined decades of experience across pharma and biotech. Headquartered in Los Altos, California. We are building and deploying the product now with rapid expansion into global markets.

   

About the Role

We're looking for an Agent Engineering Intern to build new agent-driven workflows inside Cheiron's product.

 

Cheiron's agents do more than generate an answer. They break complex objectives into steps, retrieve evidence, call tools, maintain state across long-running work, recover from failures, and produce structured results that a person can review and trust. You will own a bounded workflow and help take it from an ambiguous problem to a reliable, working product.

 

This is an Applied Engineering Role. We care about strong software fundamentals, hands-on ownership, and evidence that you have built nontrivial systems yourself. The role is best suited to undergraduate and master's students who are already serious builders.

   

What You'll Do

  • Design and implement new agent workflows with explicit state, task decomposition, tool use, and typed outputs.

  • Build retrieval and citation paths that ground important outputs in source evidence.

  • Add evaluation, tracing, retries, observability, and recovery behavior for multi-step execution.

  • Build the backend services, data models, APIs, and focused product surfaces required to make the workflow useful.

  • Test agent behavior against realistic success cases, failure cases, and incomplete evidence.

  • Work directly with engineers and domain experts, demonstrate progress frequently, and make pragmatic scope decisions.

   

Requirements

  • Currently pursuing an undergraduate or master's degree in computer science, computer engineering, or a related technical field.

  • Strong programming fundamentals and experience building a substantial software project, developer tool, backend system, or open-source contribution.

  • Hands-on experience building a nontrivial agent, retrieval system, tool-using workflow, evaluation harness, or multi-step automation system.

  • Clear personal ownership of the work: you can explain what you implemented, the decisions you made, and what you would improve.

  • Ability to reason about state, failure modes, grounding, evaluation, and engineering tradeoffs—not only prompts and model selection.

  • High agency and comfort working through ambiguous problems in a fast-moving environment.

  • Ability to work fully in person in Los Altos. Semester or quarter interns must commit at least 20 hours per week; summer interns should be available full time.

   

Nice to Have

  • Experience with Python, FastAPI, Postgres, agent frameworks, retrieval systems, or vector databases.

  • Backend, distributed-systems, infrastructure, data-pipeline, or end-to-end product experience.

  • Experience with tests, deployment, observability, security, or reliable failure handling.

  • Experience building systems involving citations, provenance, human review, or other high-stakes correctness requirements.

  • Strong open-source work, prior software-engineering internships, or an independently shipped product with real users.

   

Compensation

$35–$55 per hour. Exact compensation within the range depends on demonstrated expertise, relevant experience, and the time the student can commit.

  

Location, Relocation & Visa

This role is fully in person in Los Altos, CA. Academic-term interns must be able to work from the office at least 20 hours per week; summer interns should expect a full-time commitment. Relocation assistance may be offered selectively to a strong candidate and is not guaranteed. Candidates of any nationality or visa status may be considered when the internship can be employed legally.

  

Interview Process

Semester/quarter route:

  • 30-minute introductory call → one-day onsite in Los Altos → decision.

Summer route:

  • 15-minute introductory call → take-home assignment → take-home interview → interview with Backend Team → decision.

  • For some summer candidates, the final two interviews may instead be combined into a one-day onsite in Los Altos.

  

Equal Opportunity & Accommodation

Cheiron is an equal-opportunity employer. We consider all qualified applicants without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, age, disability, veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by law.

By prioritizing relentless hardware iteration, we deliver high-speed systems at the pace of the modern battlefield. About The Role: 

As a GNC & Flight Software Engineering Intern, you will support the development, implementation, and testing of flight software and guidance, navigation, and control systems for uncrewed high-speed aircraft. This role is a fit for candidates with either a strong software background and exposure to GNC/controls, or a strong GNC/controls background with hands-on software experience.

Spring: Around 16 weeks (January - April) Summer: Around 12 weeks (May - August)

Responsibilities:

Support the development and implementation of flight software and guidance and control algorithms Implement, integrate, and test control algorithms in simulation, embedded, and hardware-integrated environments Assist with control law development, tuning, and validation for vehicle stability and performance Develop software interfaces, messaging, and integrations between flight and mission subsystems Analyze test data, troubleshoot system behavior, and support improvements to software and control performance Collaborate across software, GNC, avionics, and vehicle engineering teams to validate integrated systems

Requirements:

Pursuing a degree in Aerospace Engineering, Computer Engineering, Computer Science, Electrical Engineering, or a related technical field Background in either software development with exposure to GNC/controls, or GNC/controls with experience implementing software Experience with C++, C, Python, MATLAB/Simulink, or similar programming and engineering tools Familiarity with controls, dynamics, simulation, embedded systems, or hardware/software integration Hands-on experience through internships, coursework, research, or technical projects Strong understanding of engineering first principles Demonstrated ability to work within cross-functional teams Excellent written and verbal communication skills GPA of 3.0 or above

The hourly rate listed for this internship is intended as a general guideline. Final compensation will be determined based on degree level.

Benefits:

  • Time Off: Interns are eligible for 5 days of sick leave and unpaid time off.
  • Office Perks: Weekly paid office lunches and fully stocked breakrooms.

We are seeking innovative engineering interns to join our team in the design and characterization of high-performance mixed-signal integrated circuits (ICs). This is a unique opportunity to work on cutting-edge technologies and critical analog/mixed-signal circuitry in state-of-the-art CMOS processes.   As an intern, you’ll collaborate with experienced engineers to solve real-world challenges, contribute to product development, and gain hands-on experience in a fast-paced, supportive environment.

We recruit interns year-round for Spring, Summer, and Fall 2027 opportunities. Each internship lasts 12–16 weeks and follows a full-time schedule.

Responsibilities

Assist in the design, simulation, and verification of mixed-signal ICs. Support characterization and testing of silicon prototypes. Analyze performance data and contribute to design improvements. Collaborate across teams to ensure robust and efficient circuit implementations.

Required Skills and Qualifications

Currently pursuing a MS or PhD in Electrical Engineering or a related field. Strong understanding of analog and digital circuit fundamentals. Experience with circuit simulation tools (e.g., Cadence, SPICE). Familiarity with lab equipment such as oscilloscopes, spectrum analyzers, and signal generators. Excellent problem-solving skills and attention to detail. Strong communication and teamwork abilities. Cirrus Logic follows a 2+ day in-office work schedule but interns should expect to be in the office more often, up to 5 days per week, based on business needs and team preference. Different approaches, ideas and points of view are both valued and respected.
